authoredPrompt: This figure shows the logistic sigmoid function sig[z] plotted as a single smooth curve over the range z ∈ [−5, 5]. The horizontal axis is labeled z with tick marks at −5.0, 0.0, and 5.0, and the vertical axis is labeled sig[z] with tick marks at 0.0 and 1.0. A smooth orange S-shaped curve rises monotonically from near zero on the left to near one on the right, with its steepest slope occurring at z = 0 where the function equals exactly 0.5. Gray dashed lines indicate the horizontal asymptote at sig[z] = 1.0 and mark a vertical reference at z = 0, emphasizing the function’s symmetry and its asymptotic approach to both bounds. This figure introduces the logistic sigmoid as a differentiable, bounded activation function that squashes any real-valued input into the interval (0, 1), motivating its use for modeling probabilities in binary classification.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag a point along the sigmoid curve to display the exact coordinate pair (z, sig[z]) at that position
- Slider for a probability threshold: draw a horizontal line at the chosen value and mark the corresponding z intercept where the sigmoid crosses it

discrepancies: the source has only light gray dotted guide segments from the y-axis to (0, 0.5) and from the x-axis to (0, 0.5), but the generated default overlays a prominent blue dashed horizontal threshold line across the entire plot and a blue vertical threshold line

the generated figure adds a large draggable open-circle point at the midpoint plus a coordinate callout, neither of which appears in the source and both visually dominate the central guide intersection
the plot area is noticeably more square and compressed horizontally because the UI panel occupies the right side, whereas the source has a wider rectangular plotting frame
the source’s unobtrusive gray midpoint guides are partly obscured/replaced by darker blue interactive threshold styling, changing the visual emphasis
the default generated image includes UI text and controls beside the plot, so it is not a clean drop-in replacement for the static textbook figure
evaluation.notes: The sigmoid curve, axes, tick labels, and formula are mostly correct, but the default state adds prominent threshold and draggable-point annotations that substantially change the source figure’s simple static composition.
action_items: Make the default guide styling match the source: light gray dotted segments only from x = -5 to 0 at y = 0.5 and from y = 0 to 0.5 at x = 0, not a blue full-width threshold line.
Hide the draggable point marker and coordinate callout by default, or make them optional through a control so the initial view matches the source figure.
Preserve the wider aspect ratio of the original plotting frame and avoid allowing the UI panel to shrink the plot into a more square layout.
Keep interaction controls visually secondary or docked away from the default screenshot area so the static figure remains recognizable as the textbook graphic.
